questions.question: True or false: Hannah was the wife of Elkanah, who lived in Ramathaim-Zophim in the hill country of Ephraim.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Elkanah, a man of the tribe of Levi, worked to revive the pilgrimage to the Tabernacle at Shiloh.

questions.question: What did Elkanah say to Hannah in order to comfort her?
options: "Am I not better to you than ten sons?"
"Do I not love you above all?"
"What have you to do with Peninnah?"
"Shall I not give you all that you ask?"
questions.explanation: He gave her "one portion, a double one," but did not understand that her pain stemmed from a religious calling: a son who would be dedicated to the Lord.

questions.question: What did Eli the priest think when he saw Hannah praying?
options: That she was ill
That she was drunk
That she was cursing
That she was a false prophetess
questions.explanation: Only her lips moved and her voice was not heard, which was so exceptional in Shiloh. She answered: "and I pour out my soul before the Lord."

questions.question: True or false: Hannah prayed at Shiloh in a loud voice, so that everyone would hear.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Her prayer was silent: "Now Hannah spoke in her heart." From this the laws of the Amidah prayer were learned.

questions.question: True or false: Eli the priest rebuked Hannah and did not bless her.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: When he realized his mistake he blessed her: "And the God of Israel grant your petition." Her face "was no longer sad."

questions.question: What did the Sages learn from the words "Now Hannah spoke in her heart"?
options: That it is forbidden to pray in Shiloh
That prayer is said in the heart alone, without the lips
That the one who prays must direct his heart
That prayer offered in private exempts one from a sacrifice
questions.explanation: The intention of the heart became the center of religious service: a transition from institutional sacrificial worship to the service of the heart.

questions.question: True or false: Hannah was the first to call God by the name "Lord of Hosts."
options: True
False
questions.explanation: "Of all the hosts upon hosts that You created in Your world, is it hard in Your eyes to give me one son?"

questions.question: Which parable did Hannah use in her prayer, according to the Sages?
options: A guest who was forgotten outside the palace
A farmer asking for rain in the summer
A servant asking for freedom from his master
A poor man asking for a small slice at a king's great feast
questions.explanation: It is no trouble for the king to give it to him. So she asked for one son from the Creator of Hosts.

questions.question: How did Hannah expound the name "Samuel"?
options: "Sha'ul me-El" ("asked of God"): the child is a deposit for his mission
After his grandfather
From the word "shemen" (oil), a hint of the anointing of kings
From the word "shem" (name), for his good name
questions.explanation: The child is not the property of his parents, but a deposit that they must prepare for his public mission.

questions.question: True or false: Hannah kept Samuel at home until he grew up, and only then brought him to the Tabernacle.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: She handed him over to the Tabernacle at Shiloh as soon as he was weaned, at the age of two or two and a half.

questions.question: What did Hannah prepare for Samuel every year?
options: A little crown
A little robe
A little Torah scroll
A little candle
questions.explanation: The robe symbolized the continuing bond between them. Even the medium recognized Samuel by his robe.

questions.question: According to the Malbim, in what did Hannah ask that Samuel differ from the other Levites?
options: That he be a high priest and a king
That he be a judge and a military commander
That he be a nazirite, dedicated from his youth, and a prophet
That he be wealthy and a poet
questions.explanation: She gave up the pleasure of raising him for the sake of his national calling.

questions.question: What were the nine blessings of the Rosh Hashanah Musaf prayer instituted to correspond to?
options: The nine months of pregnancy
The nine tribes of the north
The nine days of judgment
The nine mentions of the Name of the Lord in Hannah's prayer
questions.explanation: Hannah was remembered on Rosh Hashanah, and her story is the haftarah of the first day of the festival.

questions.question: True or false: The story of Hannah is the haftarah of the first day of Rosh Hashanah.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Hannah represents remembrance and being remembered: the Holy One, blessed be He, remembers the individual within the collective.

questions.question: With which words does the Song of Hannah end?
options: "And He shall give strength to His king, and exalt the horn of His anointed"
"The Lord shall reign forever and ever"
"The Lord will give strength to His people"
"Blessed be the Lord forever. Amen and Amen"
questions.explanation: In a period when there was no king in Israel, Hannah prophesied about the monarchy and messianism.

questions.question: What does the verse "The Lord makes poor and makes rich; He brings low, He also lifts up" express?
options: That wealth is a sign of righteousness
The principle of reversal: the Lord raises up the weak and brings down the proud
That the order of the world must not be changed
That the poor will remain poor forever
questions.explanation: History is not determined by military or economic power, but by "the God of knowledge, the Lord."

questions.question: What is the difference between "blessing" and "prayer" in Hannah's teaching, according to the research?
options: A blessing is said aloud and a prayer in a whisper
A blessing is for the priests and a prayer is for the people
A blessing draws down existing abundance; a prayer seeks to renew a will
A blessing concerns the past and a prayer concerns the present
questions.explanation: Hannah asked for a change of nature itself: that a barren woman should bear a child, and not just any child but "seed of men."

questions.question: What is the difference, according to the Sages, between anointing with a "flask" and anointing with a "horn"?
options: A flask for priests, a horn for kings
A flask in Shiloh, a horn in Jerusalem
A flask for prophets, a horn for judges
A flask (Saul, Jehu): temporary kingship; a horn (David, Solomon): eternal kingship
questions.explanation: The flask is a fragile vessel and the horn is a strong vessel. The Sages see in the song an explicit prophecy about Saul and David.

questions.question: Which "physical" argument did Hannah hurl upward, according to the Sages?
options: "Why did You create breasts in me, if not to nurse with them?"
"Why did You give to Peninnah and not to me?"
"Why did You not hear Elkanah's sacrifices?"
"Why did You create me a woman?"
questions.explanation: If the Creator made the instruments, He must enable them to fulfill their function. Prayer is not only submission, but sometimes a demand.

questions.question: According to the Midrash, what was Peninnah's intention in her taunts?
options: To take her place with Elkanah
For the sake of Heaven: to press Hannah until she would pray with all her heart
To drive Hannah away from Shiloh
To prove that her sons were worthy of the Tabernacle
questions.explanation: Peninnah, who had ten sons and daughters, behaved cruelly, but according to the Midrash her intention was that Hannah would cry out.
